_what: Pekoe and Purrs, the cat café on the street. Ryan Boren's brief, 2026-10-04: coffee, tea, tea sandwiches, and cats from the cat rescue waiting for adoption; a coffee, tea and tea sandwich menu with vegan and vegetarian options; cats from the shelter roaming the café among toys, lofts and wall playgrounds; click a cat for its name and adoption information, with a link to the rescue; the cats move around the café periodically; pick one up and put it in your lap; look down at your lap and table to see the cat in your lap and your drinks and food on the table. tools/make-pekoe.py builds the room, the menu and the credits out of this file. THE CATS ARE NOT IN THIS FILE: purrs.js reads them off the shelter's own public list (GET /cb/shelter?kind=cat) every time the room opens, so the café can never show a cat the shelter does not have, nor miss one it does.
_menu: Every item says what is in it before you ask for it. The allergen line and the diet are checked against the ingredients by the same engine Hey, Good Cookin' uses (make-hey-good-cookin.py's allergens(), animals() and check_dish()), so the two kitchens cannot disagree about a word. Every drink's caffeine line is worked out from what is in it and never typed: the runtime rule at a café counter. A drink whose ingredients name no bean, leaf, flower or chocolate is refused rather than called caffeine-free by default. The house milk is oat; `ask` is a swap somebody can ask for and is said on the card, not counted in the allergen line, which is what the item is as it comes. A drink's `look` is the colour of what is in the mug, never the mug: every mug in the café is the same mug.

_videos: THE TELLY'S RACK. Ryan's pick, 2026-10-04, in the order he gave them: films from other cat cafés, most of them in Japan. Each id was asked of its own watch page on 2026-10-04, and every one answered OK and playable on other sites; the title, the channel and the runtime are what that page said, the runtime measured off its length and never typed. The titles are the channels' and are quoted as written, capitals, emoji and all, and the room's sweeps skip them. A video is an id, a title, a channel, a runtime and the day it went up: no description and no count of views or likes, which make-pekoe.py refuses. check-jukebox.py asks after every one of them with every other facade on the street.

_table: How many things your table holds at once. Small round café tables, and a cat on your lap who would like some of the room.
_windows: THE LIGHT. A window at every height, each cut to the size of a cat, so every perch has a window of its own to look out of and each one lays a small square of day on the wall beside it. x and y are the window's centre in the drawing (1200 by 660), w and h its size. `shape` is square, round or arch. The squares of day fall down and to the right of every window, because the sun is up and to the left of the building, and they are drawn by the tool from the window, never placed by hand.
_spots: Every place a cat can be in the room. x and y are where the cat's feet go, in the drawing's 1200 by 660. `kind` says what the perch is, and the tool draws it: shelf, sill, bridge, hammock, ledge, chair, floor, basket, box, tree or cubby. `level` is high, middle or floor. `where` is what the room says out loud about a cat there. There must be more perches than the shelter can ever hold, so a cat always has somewhere to go, and the tool reads SHELTER_KEEP out of netlify/cb/lib.mjs to make sure. No two cats' places may overlap.

_moods: Where a cat goes is decided by its mood and by nothing else: the mood the shelter wrote down when it came in (CAT_MOODS in netlify/cb/lib.mjs, read by the tool, which refuses a mood with no entry here). `kinds` and `levels` narrow the perches it likes; an empty rule likes anywhere. When none it likes is free it goes wherever is free. A cat's markings are never consulted: a cat with three legs climbs to the top of the tree like anybody else, which is what 'no opinion about it' means. `toys` false is a cat a toy does not move.
_left_alone: A cat whose mood is in this list is never picked up: its card says so, with no button. The shelter wrote down that it wants to be left alone, which is allowed, and the café keeps to that. The tool refuses this list without 'alone' in it.
_toys: The toys you can wave, roll or put down. Each sends any cat whose mood likes the toy's perches, and who is not asleep or wanting to be left alone, after it. Nothing is counted.
